meta.title: Cache-Control Analyzer - S-Jiffy
meta.description: Parse HTTP Cache-Control headers and explain the meaning of each directive
desc: Parse HTTP Cache-Control headers and explain the meaning of each directive
ui.4: If the origin server returns an error, stale cached responses may be used for the specified time.
ui.5: The client will only accept cached content and will not load from the origin server. Returns 504 if not in cache.
ui.6: Specifies which fields in the response must not be stored.
ui.7: Caches must understand and honor all caching directives in the response; otherwise the response must not be stored.
ui.8: The resource content never changes and needs no revalidation before expiry. Suitable for fingerprinted static assets.
ui.9: Shared caches (proxies) must revalidate with the origin server after the resource expires. Private browser caches are unaffected.
ui.10: Once the cache expires, it must be revalidated with the origin server before use. Stale cache must not be used even if the proxy is unavailable.
ui.11: Intermediate proxies or CDNs must not apply any transformation to the resource content (e.g., compression, transcoding).
ui.12: No cache may store any part of this request or response. Caching is completely forbidden.
ui.13: The cache must revalidate the resource with the origin server before serving it to the client. A conditional request is required each time.
ui.14: The response may only be stored in private browser caches; shared caches (such as CDNs) must not cache it.
ui.15: Any cache (including shared caches) may cache this response, even if the response normally requires authentication.
ui.16: Maximum time (seconds) shared caches (e.g., CDNs, proxies) may hold the response; takes precedence over max-age. Applies to public caches only.
ui.17: The maximum time (seconds) a response may be cached. After this, the cache must revalidate with the origin server.
ui.100: Please enter a Cache-Control header value
